entries.title: ALMA finds a fully heavy version of methanol around a young star
entries.excerpt: ALMA has detected CD₃OD, a rare form of methanol in which every hydrogen atom is replaced by heavier deuterium, around a young star about 1,000 light-years away. Its chemical fingerprint challenges models of how molecules form in the cold clouds that give birth to stars.

entries.title: Slow freezing sorts the salts in Enceladus's ocean spray
entries.excerpt: Cassini found that salt-rich ice grains from Enceladus do not all carry the same chemical mix. Laboratory experiments now suggest that large ocean droplets freeze slowly inside the moon's vents, separate their salts, and then shatter into distinct grains on the way to space.

entries.title: Garro 04 is a hidden star cluster that resists a neat label
entries.excerpt: Infrared observations have revealed Garro 04, a real group of stars hidden in the crowded disk of the Milky Way. At about 5 billion years old, it falls into an awkward gap between the usual open and globular cluster categories.

entries.title: Webb finds warm dust around a quiet black hole binary
entries.excerpt: Webb measured an unexpected mid-infrared glow from the dormant black hole binary XTE J1118+480. The spectrum fits warm dust better than the steady compact jet usually invoked for faint black hole systems, suggesting material may survive in a ring outside the binary.

entries.excerpt: A gamma-ray burst's four-second flash left its source unclear after ground telescopes found no accompanying supernova. Webb separated a faint, dust-reddened supernova from its bright host galaxy, tying the burst to the collapse of a massive star.

entries.title: Methane glows from a six-Jupiter-mass brown dwarf
entries.excerpt: Webb detected two infrared emission lines from methane in a young brown dwarf weighing about six Jupiters. Methane usually leaves absorption features in cool atmospheres, so the glow points to unusual heating or radiation high above this object's visible surface.

entries.title: A sub-Neptune circles its red dwarf backwards
entries.excerpt: GJ 3090 b is the first planet found on a retrograde orbit around an M-dwarf star. Its strongly tilted path is hard to explain with the usual massive-companion scenarios, pointing instead toward a planet-forming disk that may have started out misaligned.

entries.title: One Martian rock unit records three separate water episodes
entries.excerpt: Perseverance found that an olivine-rich rock unit beside Jezero Crater's ancient lake records at least three distinct encounters with water. The sequence includes carbon dioxide-rich groundwater, lake-related alteration, and a later pulse of hot underground fluid.
